messages:
maria: Heads-up: I found a `debug-artifacts/2026-03-17/trace.tar.gz` uploaded to our staging S3 bucket that contains a `env/credentials.env` file with SERVICE_API_KEY inside. Not sure how it got packaged — profiling job maybe. Can someone advise redaction + rotation steps? cc @kevin @anya
security-bot: Alert: Detected potential secret in S3 object staging-debug/trace.tar.gz — recommended action: revoke key, remove object, and set object to private.
kevin: Thanks — can you paste the S3 path + object version? We'll need to expunge the object ASAP.
maria: s3://redwood-staging-debug/debug-artifacts/trace-20260317.tar.gz (version v3). I grabbed a quick listing: `tar -tzf trace-20260317.tar.gz | grep env` and saw `credentials.env`
anya: If key is valid we should rotate. Who owns the service? Is it a short-lived service token from Vault or a long-lived KMS-wrapped API key?
maria: It's the worker service using a Vault-stored API key injected at startup (VAULT_SECRET=svc/worker/api_key:v2). But the dumped file contained the raw key.
sam: OK plan: 1) remove object from S3 (secure delete if possible) 2) create a new secret version in Vault for svc/worker/api_key 3) rotate KMS wrap if wrapped, or rewrap 4) update staging deployment with new secret 5) audit and TTL any long-lived tokens. Security can approve emergency rotation.
kevin: Agree. Also add object-level audits: enable S3 object lock? For now just set ACL private and delete plus file reupload prevention. Use `aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-staging-debug --key debug-artifacts/trace-20260317.tar.gz --version-id v3`
maria: done: I removed the object and filed an internal incident ticket #INC-4721. I didn't download the file locally after the scan.
security-bot: Incident #INC-4721 created. Remediation checklist: revoke/exchange leaked key, confirm deletion, rotate secrets, run re-scan.
anya: I can approve rotation. Maria, please open a Vault version bump for svc/worker/api_key and tag me in the PR. Also add an action to update the CI/CD to exclude `/tmp/debug/*.tar.gz` from uploads.
maria: Will do. Quick Q: who performs the actual key rotation? infra oncall or the service owner?
kevin: Service owner should rotate (they know rollouts). If owner unavailable infra-oncall can rotate as emergency but must hand off.
sam: Note: if the key was KMS-wrapped, rewrapping is optional if you rotate the underlying secret in Vault — but if KMS grants were leaked, rewrap & rotate keys with KMS key rotation.
anya: Also add a short postmortem to explain how debug bundle got collected; likely profiling job ran with DEBUG=true. We should block debug uploads from staging by default.
maria: Thanks all — opening PR and pinging owner. I'll update incident with steps and close once verified.
kevin: :thumbsup:
